## {#slide-03}

::: {.slide-head}
[The usual pitch]{.eyebrow}

[Why Portolan]{.headline}
:::

::: {.slide-body}
```{=html}
<div class="cols">
  <div class="a-rise" style="--d:0.2s">
    <h3>Open and interoperable</h3>
    <p>Built on GeoParquet, PMTiles, COG, and STAC, so data drops straight into QGIS, ArcGIS, pandas, or BigQuery.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="a-rise" style="--d:0.45s">
    <h3>Simple, cheap, scalable, sovereign</h3>
    <p>Your data are just files in a bucket. Any S3-compatible provider, any jurisdiction. You pay for storage and egress — no servers, no databases, no custom APIs.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="a-rise" style="--d:0.7s">
    <h3>Built for people and agents</h3>
    <p>Catalogs are well-structured, well-formatted, and well-documented, so people and agents can find, understand, and use them.</p>
  </div>
</div>
```
:::

::: {.notes}
Most of our slides look like this — which is really just trumpeting the benefits of CNG. So a common reaction from people already deep in CNG is: "why do we need this?"

And if you already know everything about CNG, and you stay up to date on the exact settings of all the formats, and you always make amazing catalogs — then the answer is, you don't.
:::


## {#slide-04}

::: {.center-v}
[Portolan is for everyone else.]{.statement .a-rise style="--d:0.3s"}

[A Portolan catalog is a STAC catalog — with more guidance, plus requirements on the CNG formats inside it, so that everything performs in a browser.]{.lead .a-fade style="--d:1.6s" }
:::

::: {.notes}
Portolan is for everyone else.

A Portolan catalog is a STAC catalog, with more guidance, plus requirements on the CNG formats that are in it to ensure they perform well in a browser.
:::


## {#slide-05}

::: {.slide-head}
[Anatomy]{.eyebrow}

[STAC, plus the rules that make it work everywhere]{.headline}
:::

::: {.slide-body .split}
```{=html}
<pre class="tree a-fade" style="--d:0.2s">catalog.json          <span class="c">STAC root</span>
├── <span class="k">AGENTS.md</span>         <span class="c">how an agent should use this data</span>
├── <span class="k">README.md</span>         <span class="c">how a person should</span>
└── collections/
    └── land-use/
        ├── collection.json
        ├── <span class="k">style.json</span>    <span class="c">MapLibre style, as an asset</span>
        ├── land-use.pmtiles
        ├── land-use.parquet
        └── parts/<span class="k">*.parquet</span>  <span class="c">glob, via the partition ext.</span></pre>
<ul class="ruled a-fade" style="--d:0.8s">
  <li><b>Required formats.</b> <span class="note">GeoParquet, PMTiles, COG — at settings that actually stream.</span></li>
  <li><b>Required documentation.</b> <span class="note">Every collection says what it is and where it came from.</span></li>
  <li><b>Required extensions.</b> <span class="note">Table extension on tabular data, so columns are known up front.</span></li>
  <li><b>A validator.</b> <span class="note"><code>portolan check</code> fails the build when any of that slips.</span></li>
</ul>
```
:::

::: {.notes}
Structurally there's not much to it. It's STAC, with a handful of things made mandatory: the formats and their settings, the documentation, the table extension, and a validator that enforces all of it.
:::


## {#slide-06}

::: {.slide-head}
[The browser]{.eyebrow}

[Replacing the portal, not wrapping it]{.headline}
:::

::: {.slide-body}
```{=html}
<figure class="shot">
  <video class="screen" src="media/data-browser.mp4" data-autoplay muted loop playsinline></video>
  <figcaption>portolan-browser, reading a catalog straight out of object storage</figcaption>
</figure>
```
:::

::: {.notes}
Our goal is to enable CNG to completely replace the traditional spatial data infrastructure APIs and portals. So we take a holistic lens on the ecosystem, to make sure we have all the pieces to deliver a complete experience.
:::


## {#slide-07}

::: {.slide-head}
[Vector in the browser]{.eyebrow}

[Making vector data actually work]{.headline}
:::

::: {.slide-body .split}
```{=html}
<figure class="shot" style="flex:1.35 1 0">
  <div class="placeholder">Placeholder — vector-in-the-browser recording</div>
</figure>
<ul class="ruled a-fade" style="--d:0.3s">
  <li><b>Styles as STAC assets.</b> <span class="note">A collection ships the cartography it was meant to be seen with.</span></li>
  <li><b>Glob syntax in the partition extension.</b> <span class="note">Point at a split dataset without listing every part.</span></li>
  <li><b>The table extension, required.</b> <span class="note">A client knows the schema before it fetches a byte.</span></li>
</ul>
```
:::

::: {.notes}
This has led to a few advances that are interesting to people in this room: including styles as assets in a STAC catalog, extending the STAC partition extension with glob syntax, and requiring the table extension.
:::


## {#slide-08}

::: {.slide-head}
[stac-geoparquet]{.eyebrow}

[Cloud-native search, with no search API]{.headline}
:::

::: {.slide-body .split}
```{=html}
<figure class="shot" style="flex:2 1 0">
  <video class="screen" src="media/s2-search.mp4" data-autoplay muted loop playsinline></video>
</figure>
<div class="stats" style="flex-direction:column; gap:2.4rem">
  <div><span class="num">20 h</span><span class="label">before</span></div>
  <div><span class="num">16 min</span><span class="label">after</span></div>
  <div><span class="num">&lt; 1 s</span><span class="label">search, full S-2 archive</span></div>
</div>
```
:::

::: {.notes}
We're embracing stac-geoparquet to enable completely cloud-native search. I just put up all of Sentinel-2 in GeoParquet, and it took a bulk processing job I had from 20 hours down to 16 minutes. And you can see it also powering sub-second search responses across the entire Sentinel-2 archive.
:::


## {#slide-09}

::: {.slide-head}
[AGENTS.md]{.eyebrow}

[Point an agent at a catalog and it just works]{.headline}
:::

::: {.slide-body .split}
```{=html}
<figure class="shot" style="flex:1.3 1 0">
  <video class="screen" src="media/tulip-chat.mp4" data-autoplay muted loop playsinline></video>
</figure>
<p class="lead a-fade" style="--d:0.4s">Almost any agent can install DuckDB and do fairly advanced geospatial analysis. The catalog just has to tell it how. We think this is what finally opens geospatial up to many more users.</p>
```
:::

::: {.notes}
And we added an AGENTS.md file, which enables pretty magical direct interaction with geospatial data. Most every agent can install DuckDB and do pretty advanced geospatial analysis, and we believe this will ultimately open up the power of geospatial to many more users.
:::


## {#slide-10}

::: {.slide-head}
[Skills and connectors]{.eyebrow}

[Making a great catalog is now the easy part]{.headline}
:::

::: {.slide-body .split}
```{=html}
<figure class="shot" style="flex:1.15 1 0">
  <video class="screen" src="media/catalog-demo.mp4" data-autoplay muted loop playsinline></video>
</figure>
<ul class="ruled a-fade" style="--d:0.4s">
  <li><b>Agentic skills</b> <span class="note">that translate an entire catalog into Portolan.</span></li>
  <li><b>Connectors</b> <span class="note">for ArcGIS, WFS, and more, getting better every week.</span></li>
  <li><b>One prompt</b> <span class="note">from a city open-data portal to a published, documented catalog.</span></li>
</ul>
```
:::

::: {.notes}
We've also invested in various agentic skills to make it easy to translate entire catalogs into Portolan, and we're continually improving the connectors to ArcGIS, WFS and others. So making a great catalog is incredibly easy.
:::


## {#slide-11}

::: {.slide-head}
[The whole stack]{.eyebrow}

[A complete ecosystem, built on your work]{.headline}
:::

::: {.slide-body}
```{=html}
<div class="eco">
  <div class="a-rise" style="--d:0.15s">
    <span class="n">01</span>
    <h3>Spec + validator</h3>
    <p>One document that says what good looks like, and a checker that enforces it.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="a-rise" style="--d:0.35s">
    <span class="n">02</span>
    <h3>CLI + skills</h3>
    <p>Convert, partition, document, and publish — by hand or by agent.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="a-rise" style="--d:0.55s">
    <span class="n">03</span>
    <h3>Browser</h3>
    <p>A portal experience served from static files, for any compliant catalog.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="a-rise" style="--d:0.75s">
    <span class="n">04</span>
    <h3>Registry</h3>
    <p>Where the catalogs are, so people and agents can find them.</p>
  </div>
</div>
```

[Still targeting early adopters. The goal: every geospatial tool understands Portolan, and hundreds of open-data catalogs exist in the format.]{.lead .a-fade style="--d:1s"}
:::

::: {.notes}
We are aiming for a complete ecosystem, and we've been leveraging all the amazing work that this community has created. We're still targeting early adopters, and our goal is to have every geospatial tool understand Portolan, and to get hundreds of catalogs of open data in the format.
:::

## {#slide-13}

::: {.slide-head}
[What the data makes possible]{.eyebrow}

[Twenty years of global fire detections, interactive]{.headline}
:::

::: {.slide-body}
```{=html}
<figure class="shot">
  <video class="screen" src="media/firms-explorer.mp4" data-autoplay muted loop playsinline></video>
  <figcaption>an explorer built on a Portolan catalog of NASA FIRMS data</figcaption>
</figure>
```
:::

::: {.notes}
With each new dataset converted, I hope we push the cloud-native geospatial ecosystem forward in a different way — that it becomes a community of people making great data products and pushing the edges of what's possible with CNG. This was an explorer I made on top of a FIRMS fire data catalog, pushing the bounds of interactivity across twenty years of global data.
:::


## {#slide-14}

::: {.slide-head}
[The registry]{.eyebrow}

[Like STAC Index, with a guarantee attached]{.headline}
:::

::: {.slide-body}
```{=html}
<figure class="shot">
  <video class="screen" src="media/registry.mp4" data-autoplay muted loop playsinline></video>
  <figcaption>every registered catalog is documented, validated, and performant</figcaption>
</figure>
```
:::

::: {.notes}
The other key bit of the ecosystem is the Portolan Registry, where all high quality catalogs get registered for everyone to query. It's like STAC Index, but with a guarantee to users that the data will always be well-documented and performant.
:::


## {#slide-15}

::: {.slide-head}
[Why the registry matters]{.eyebrow}

[Five catalogs, one question, no GIS team]{.headline}
:::

::: {.slide-body .split}
```{=html}
<figure class="shot" style="flex:1.9 1 0">
  <video class="screen" src="media/finland-demo.mp4" data-autoplay muted loop playsinline></video>
</figure>
<p class="lead a-fade" style="--d:0.4s">Siting a data centre in Finland: grid access, flood hazard, cooling water, protected areas, land cover. Previously a team of geospatial experts and a week of work.</p>
```
:::

::: {.notes}
The goal is to gather enough global data to be able to answer complex geospatial questions with LLMs. We want to enable the type of analysis that would previously take a team of geospatial experts to pull in all the data and extract insights from. This was an early demo showing how you can answer questions about data centres by pulling data in from five different Portolan catalogs.
:::


## {#slide-16}

::: {.center-v}
[We want to see all the world's data in CNG formats.]{.statement .a-rise style="--d:0.2s"}

[AI can help us get there — and the world's data in CNG formats lets anyone use AI to get geospatial insights. That's a couple of orders of magnitude more people using geospatial information.]{.lead .a-fade style="--d:1.4s"}
:::

::: {.notes}
We want to see all the world's data in CNG formats. We believe AI can help get us there, and that the world's data in CNG formats will enable anyone to use AI to get geospatial insights — increasing the users of geospatial information by at least a couple of orders of magnitude.
:::


## {#slide-17}

::: {.slide-head}
[What comes after]{.eyebrow}

[Then we go back across the chasm]{.headline}

::: {.slide-body}

<ol class="ruled" style="max-width:1180px">

:::
